key_insight: For D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr on DSS 2205, a longer spray distance of 190 mm produced the densest coating and the best acid corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray distance is a practical lever for improving coating integrity and extending the life of stainless steel components in aggressive acidic service.
method: D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr onto DSS 2205 at 170, 180, and 190 mm stand-off distances.
Assessed coating structure with SEM and porosity measurements.
Evaluated corrosion behavior in 1 M H2SO4 using OCP, EIS, and potentiodynamic polarization.
evidence_signal: Porosity decreased from 2.84% at 170 mm to 1.38% at 190 mm, and the 190 mm coating showed the lowest corrosion rate at 0.113 mmpy versus 2.60 mmpy for the uncoated substrate.
watch_item: The optimum distance was established for one coating system and one acid environment, so transfer to other substrates, gases, or service conditions should be validated experimentally.
paper_title: Effect of spray distance in D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings on DSS 2205 in acidic environments
